groups.title: Node.js Runtime Internals
groups.question: Explain how Node.js serves many requests at once on a single thread, and how async errors move through your code.

followUps.The Event Loop & Non-blocking I/O: What happens to every other request when one handler runs a heavy synchronous loop?
followUps.Promises, async/await & Error Propagatio: Where does an error thrown inside an async function end up, and what happens if nobody catches it?

evidence.text: JavaScript callbacks run on one main thread; I/O is handed off and its callback runs when the result is ready.
A long synchronous computation blocks that thread, so every other request waits until it finishes.
Heavy CPU work should be split up or moved to worker threads or another process.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (event loop, non-blocking, libuv) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says Node gives each request its own thread, so a slow handler only slows its own request.

evidence.text: An error thrown inside an async function rejects the promise that function returns.
It is caught by try/catch around an await, or by .catch on the promise.
If nothing handles it, it becomes an unhandled rejection, which crashes the process in current Node versions.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (async/await, promises, try/catch) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says a try/catch catches errors from an async call even when the call isn't awaited.

groups.title: Node.js Module System
groups.question: Explain how code is split into modules in Node.js, and what Node gives you without installing anything.

followUps.ESM vs CommonJS — Module Resolution: What is the difference between require and import, and why do they clash in the same project?
followUps.Built-in Modules — fs, path, http, strea: Why would you stream a large file instead of reading it all with fs.readFile?

evidence.text: CommonJS uses require and module.exports; ESM uses import and export.
Node decides which one a file uses from its extension (.mjs/.cjs) or the type field in package.json.
They don't mix freely: require isn't defined in ESM, and CommonJS can't simply require an ESM-only package.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (require, import, ESM, CommonJS) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says import is only newer syntax for require and the two always work together.

evidence.text: Node ships core modules like fs, path, http and stream that need no install.
Streaming reads the file in small chunks, so memory stays low however large the file is, and sending can start right away.
readFile loads the whole file into memory first, which is slow or fails for large files.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (fs, stream, readFile) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says readFile already streams the file in the background.

groups.title: npm & Dependency Management
groups.question: Explain how a Node project manages its dependencies and common tasks.

followUps.package.json, Semantic Versioning & Lock: What does ^1.4.0 allow npm to install, and why does the lock file need to be committed?
followUps.npm Scripts & Workspaces: Why run tools through npm scripts instead of installing them globally?

evidence.text: Versions are major.minor.patch, and a major bump signals breaking changes.
^1.4.0 allows any 1.x version from 1.4.0 upward, but not 2.0.0.
The committed lock file pins the exact version of every dependency, so every machine and CI installs the same tree.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (semver, package-lock, caret) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

evidence.text: npm scripts run tools from the project's own node_modules, so nothing needs a global install.
Everyone and CI use the same tool version, the one pinned in package.json.
One named command, like npm run test or npm run build, works the same everywhere.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (npm scripts, package.json) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says npm scripts only work if the tool is installed globally.

groups.title: Debugging Node.js
groups.question: Explain how you would track down a bug, or a server whose memory keeps growing, in a Node.js API.

followUps.Node.js Inspector & VS Code Debugger: What can a breakpoint show you that console.log can't, especially in async code?
followUps.Memory Profiling & Heap Snapshots: How would heap snapshots help you find what is leaking memory?

evidence.text: A breakpoint pauses the program so you can inspect every variable and the call stack at that moment.
You can step through the code, including into async callbacks, without editing and rerunning it.
console.log only shows what you decided to print in advance.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (breakpoints, inspector, debugger) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says breakpoints only work in browser code, not in Node.

evidence.text: A heap snapshot records the objects in memory at one moment.
Comparing snapshots taken over time shows which kinds of objects keep growing.
The retainer path shows what still references them, such as a listener, closure, cache or open connection.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (heap snapshot, memory leak) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says memory leaks can't happen in JavaScript because of garbage collection.
